title: Workbook: Heat Related Illness Dashboard Live
bodyText:
Emergency Department Visits for Heat-Related Illness
Last Updated: 9/3/2026    
Purpose
The Occupational Heat-Related Illness Prevention Program monitors emergency department (ED) visits for heat-related illness (HRI) to determine the effect of extreme heat on people seeking healthcare in Louisiana.


Heat-Related Illness
HRI, or hyperthermia, occurs when the body cannot cool itself sufficiently through sweating. HRI ranges in severity from mild such as heat rash and heat cramps, to severe such as heat exhaustion and heatstroke.
Data Description
ED visits for HRI are selected if the medical record contains text or a diagnostic code associated with heat exhaustion, heat or sun exposure, heat cramps, heat stroke or hyperthermia. 


Shown below are the daily number of HRI Emergency Department visits (for residents and out of state visitors) to EDs in Louisiana and cumulative counts by age, sex, race, ethnicity, LDH region, day of the week, and time of day. Data presented are preliminary and may have slight variations each week.  


Reporting Period
Data refreshes weekly on Thursdays, April – October.
